title: AT citation check: a bare id line on another thread's arm satisfies a same-numbered row, so a row passes with no id over its own arm
body:
**AN AT ROW PASSES THE CONTRACT WHEN THE FILE IT CITES CARRIES THE SAME-NUMBERED ID ON ANOTHER THREAD'S ARM, AS LONG AS THAT LINE NAMES NO THREAD.** So a row can read green with no id over its own arm. 0267 scoped the check to the thread and kept the bare id line green on purpose; this is the case that choice lets through.

Raised by intent-vc on hv's Ok (devbin todo 190), from devbin-vc's report. intent-vc re-read each line of the evidence below in Devbin's tree on rhadamanth on 2026-10-31, with Intent 3.2.8 (brew, b14e2745632d).

**The evidence, in Devbin's tree.**

- Devbin ST0011's row AT-3.5 cites `tests/unit/releasestatus.bats`, covers AC-3.3 and reads green. Its note names the file's WP06 arm, "a tag whose object the repository lacks stops release status with git's own words", which is the test at line 161. No line over that test carries `AT-3.5`.
- The file's one line containing `AT-3.5` is line 490, `# AT-3.5`, over the test "every row is rendered by release_row, the function a cut's summary will call", in the section headed `ONE RENDERER (AC-3.1)`. The file's header names it as ST0007 WP-03's, and ST0007's own AT-3.5 cites the file and covers AC-3.1 (`intent ac status ST0007`: 20/20 satisfied, PASS).
- `intent ac status ST0011` reads `BLOCKED -- 21 acceptance test contract finding(s) over 22 row(s)`, each one `<file> does not carry the literal id AT-x.y`. AT-3.5 is the 22nd row, and it passes on ST0007's line.

**The mechanism, read by intent-vc in Intent's tree at a06ac2cd1.**

- The contract calls `refs.carries_id(path, &t.id, &thread.id)` for each row (`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/contract.rs:848`).
- `RepoFiles::carries_id` (`contract.rs:344-367`) collects every line that contains the id and answers `Yes` when any of them does not name another thread. `names_another_thread` (`contract.rs:262-265`) is false for a line that names no thread at all, so a bare `# AT-3.5` counts for every thread whose row cites the file.
- That shape is 0267's, chosen on purpose. Its comment (`contract.rs:336-343`) says a line naming no thread "carries no evidence of belonging elsewhere", and that requiring a thread-qualified id would have reddened 160 of the 196 rows the check applied to. In a file that two threads share, the bare line does belong elsewhere, and nothing on the line can say so.
- Read, not driven: the match is `line.contains(at_id)` (`contract.rs:348`), so a line carrying only `AT-3.50` would also count for `AT-3.5`.

**Why it matters.** The literal id is the coverage mechanism, not a naming convention (`contract.rs:307-313`): it is how the gate knows the cited file tests this criterion. Here it reports coverage the cited arm does not have. In ST0011, the 21 rows that fail are honest, and the one that passes is the one whose own arm carries no id.

**What a fix has to decide**, which is the reporter's to rule.

- devbin-vc's recommendation, which intent-vc shares: the check looks for the id over the thread's own arm, or the row cites the arm's line (eg `tests/unit/releasestatus.bats:161`), so the gate reads the id where the arm is.
- Either way, a bare line on another thread's arm stops counting, which is the case 0267's comment set aside. Measuring how many rows that reddens across the estate comes first, as it did for 0267.

**Measured by intent-vc on 2026-11-01, read-only, at 06:58Z on intent-vc's date -u, for hv's ruling on the shape.** The check applies today to 404 AT rows across the 32 Intent projects on rhadamanth that keep threads: rows of kind test, green or red, citing a file, on a thread that is not completed. 383 pass and 21 fail, and the 21 are Devbin ST0011's. Among the 404, a fix reddens 1 row, the exhibit above, if a bare line stops counting only where another thread has a green or red row of the same id citing the same file. It reddens 14 if a bare line stops counting wherever another thread cites the file, 116 if every carrying line must name its thread, and 383 if every row must say where its arm is with no fallback. Matching the id as a whole token, so that `AT-3.5` is no longer found inside `AT-3.50`, reddens none. Completed threads are exempt from the check, so no shape reddens a row there while its thread stays closed. The real `intent at lint` agreed with the census on every examined count and every finding on 10 threads and 129 rows. The readout, the scripts and their outputs are banked at `refs/bank/vc/0670/`, and the readout is blob d9ebd8d192f7.

**Ruled by hv on 2026-11-01, by selection in the TUI in devbin-vc's window, relayed by devbin-vc (received by 07:10Z on intent-vc's date -u): "ambiguous lines stop", the 1-row shape measured above.** A bare id line stops counting only where another thread has a green or red row of the same id citing the same file, and such a row then cites its arm as `file:line`. Once the fix ships, Devbin ST0011's AT-3.5 cites its arm as `file:line`. The relay's words were "a row of the same id"; devbin-vc confirmed that hv chose the shape as measured, on green or red rows, the rows whose arms exist. Counted on rows of any status, it would also redden Gtools ST0019 AT-07.6, whose only rival is ST0018's to-write row on a completed thread, and it does not.

**Delivery, on two rulings of hv's, recorded by intent-vc on 2026-11-10.** On 2026-11-01, by selection in intent-vc's TUI, answered by 10:05Z on intent-vc's date -u, hv ruled that this issue is built after Devbin's ST0011 ships and rides the release after 3.2.9 (vc decision 105). On 2026-11-10, first-hand in prose in intent-vc's session, read by 09:06Z on intent-vc's date -u, hv ruled that one release, 3.3.0, carries everything outstanding and that there is no 3.2.9 (hv directive 1, vc decision 109). So this issue rides 3.3.0. It no longer waits for Devbin's ST0011, which closes only at Intent's first cut through devbin's release core, and that cut is 3.3.0 itself (intent-vc's reading under the pen, open to hv's reversal). intent-dc builds it once ST0091's packages are on main. intent-vc judges it with the census at `refs/bank/vc/0670/` run again against the build, which must redden Devbin ST0011 AT-3.5 and nothing else.

**The shape of the build, ruled by intent-vc under hv's pen on 2026-11-10, in answer to intent-dc's two questions of 2026-11-01** (`refs/bank/dc/0670/shape-questions.md`). Each point is open to hv's reversal.

- Rivals. A row's rivals are the rows of kind test, status green or red, with the same id, on any other thread of the project whatever that thread's status, citing the same path as written once any `:<line>` is taken off either side. That is the census's `armed` set, and intent-dc read it the same way. A thread's status is ignored because the exhibit's rival, ST0007, is completed.
- A bare id line. Where a row has a rival, a line that carries the id and names no thread stops counting for it. A line that names the row's own thread counts, as it does today, and a line that names only other threads does not, as today.
- A row that cites `<file>:<line>`. The path is what L2 resolves, through one parser that the gate, the existence refusal of `at red` and `at green`, and doctor's finding for an absent citation all use. L3 then reads that one line and no other: the row passes when the line carries the id and does not name only other threads. A bare id there counts even where the row has rivals, because the row has said which line is its own, and nothing elsewhere in the file counts for such a row. intent-dc recommended a wider read, the cited line and the lines directly above it back to the first blank line. intent-vc took the one line for three reasons. It needs no rule about a file's layout. Under the wider read, two arms with no blank line between them let a rival's line count. And a read can be widened later without turning any row red, where narrowing one cannot.
- The refusals. A row refused for an ambiguous bare line is told the rival threads and both remedies: name this thread on the line that carries the id over its own arm, or cite that line as `<file>:<line>`. A `<file>:<line>` row refused because its line does not carry the id is told the line it asked for and the lines of the file that do carry the id, so a citation left stale by an edit is corrected from the refusal.
- Whole-token matching rides with it. The id is matched as a whole token by the census's own test, that the character after the id is not a digit, so `AT-3.5` is no longer found inside `AT-3.50`. The census measured that this reddens no row. hv's ruling chose which rows redden and this adds none, so it is intent-vc's addition under the pen and not part of hv's ruling.
- Every reader of a citation takes the new form. The bank names each place that reads a row's cited path, in Rust, in the shell guards and in the app, and shows that each one takes `<file>:<line>` or never sees one.
- The CHANGELOG entry goes under 3.3.0's `### Fixed`, and the help of the `at` verbs and the generated guide say that a row may cite a line.

RESOLVED FOR 3.3.0 in 03a820eb0 (dc built it to hv's ruling of 2026-11-01 and vc's shape of 2026-11-10; judged by vc in the train 0665, 0670, 0649, landed after 0665's a08b6f03e).

WHAT THE CHECK NOW DOES.
- A row's cited id counts only on a line that carries the id as a whole token and names no other thread. A bare id line stops counting for a row where another thread has a green or red row of the same id citing the same file; the refusal names that thread and both remedies, naming the row's own thread on the line or citing the arm as `<file>:<line>`. A to-write row is no rival, because it has no arm yet.
- A row may cite `<file>:<line>`, and then that one line is read. One parser, `contract::citation`, reads a line only from a positive decimal suffix; any other suffix stays part of the path.
- `ProjectRefs` carries the rival rows to every reader: the close gate, `at lint`, `at new` and `at edit`, and doctor's two arms. The ST0056 parity tools read the same suffix through `lib_citation.sh`, and the published schema faces describe the line form (SCHEMA_VERSION stays 33).

WHAT IT REDDENS. Read-only on copies of the fleet's nine projects, comparing 3.2.8 with the build: one line changes in 25 threads, Devbin ST0011 AT-3.5, as ruled.

THE SHARED TEST FIXTURE changed with it. `Fixture::write_thread` now writes each cited stub line naming its own thread and keeps the lines other threads wrote, because seeded estates gave three threads one green AT-03.1 over a bare line, the ambiguity the check refuses. vc's whole-suite judge found it, and the test stayed as strict as it was.

THE ATTACHMENTS CARRIED WITH IT. The same commit carried ST0056's five edited parity tools (absent_at_check.sh, declared_kind_check.sh, instrument_reach_census.sh, runner_roster_check.sh, stale_at_check.sh) and the new lib_citation.sh into the store as ST0056 attachments, so the store and the files on disk agree. A running intentd took in two of the six (stale_at_check.sh and lib_citation.sh) from disk before their attach ran, which vc accepted; a three-way check of canon, store and disk was green at landing. vc verified the train at 43a3d8303: attachment_drift_detected passed whole, its estate arm included.
